questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important to me, that I could have my mandatory courses from my bachelors, which was possible in Lissabon. It was for instance possible for me to have Economic History, and advanced Microeconomics lll. Also the culture, weather and social aspects were important - and how many from economic institute was sent.

Additional comments:

questions.answer: It was a little difficult, it took more time than i expected.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a welcoming week, and then after there were opening hours, where you could come and get help.

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find in Lissabon - my biggest advice is to start in good time. The good and cheap apartments are taken fast, so it's good to be in good time.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you go to Lissabon, most of exchange students live off campus, because the campus is far away. So many people live in the city, and then you can take the train together to the school. I would also advice for people to look for student housing, so you are living with other exchange students. That makes it more fun, because you can experience everything together.

questions.answer: It takes more time than i expected it too.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was easier as a bachelor student, there were many problems for the master students. Only annoying thing, was that they changed the courses from the previous year, which meant I had to change my pre-approval course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be well prepared, and take your time.

questions.answer: Just sit beside of them at lectures

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not many.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) It was very easy to get friends, because there are a lot of international students. My host university teaches only in english, which ment many international student go to that school. Also, there are many Danish students from both KU and CBS. 

2) Lisbon have very good surf conditions, so get a surf card and use your time at the waves! It's the best feeling in the morning. 

3)Lisbon has a good night-/ city life. So it is easy to go out, meet nice and sweet people (people are very friendly), and there were many cool places. In Lisbon there is a very big techno vibe.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared that there is a lot of attendance on the school. There are many school assignments, presentations and midterms.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I got.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To be alone in a big city - it was very rewarding.

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
